title: Mighty Little Bheem and the big pot.
lines: In a little village in India lives a baby.
He wears only a nappy and a little orange scarf.
He has a little tuft of hair on top of his head.
But Bheem isn't just any baby.
And when he falls, it's the ground that breaks, not Bheem.
His mummy is in the kitchen.
Those are round, sweet balls, yellow and yummy.
Mummy puts the laddoos in a big copper pot.
And she puts the pot high up on the top shelf.
Because they're for the party tonight.
Bheem stays at home with Grandma.
But Grandma falls asleep in her chair.
He looks at the pot again.
He stretches out his little arm.
But then he has an idea.
If he can't get to the pot, the pot will have to come to him.
But Bheem is so strong that the whole cupboard slides across the room.
Bheem catches it with one hand.
But then he hears something outside.
The goat is stuck in the well behind the house.
Bheem crawls outside, with the pot under his arm.
The goat is right at the bottom, in the water.
He lowers the bucket down to the goat.
The goat jumps into the bucket.
He pulls so hard that the bucket shoots up like a rocket.
The goat flies through the air.
Then children from the village come running.
The goat belongs to a little girl, Chutki.
She gives Bheem a little kiss on the cheek.
Bheem laughs and points at the pot.
One for Chutki, one for every child from the village.
Then Mummy comes back from the market.
She sees the cupboard in the middle of the room.
She sees all the children with sugar on their faces.
But then Chutki tells her what happened.
About the goat in the well.
She picks Bheem up and gives him a big hug.
Then I'll just make new laddoos for the party.
That evening there's a big party in the village.
With lights, music and lots and lots of laddoos.
He's sitting on Grandma's lap, with a laddoo in each hand.
Because rescuing and sharing make you tired.
